speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a dermatological concern; please describe the appearance, location, and duration of the skin lesion you are worried about. To help me evaluate its potential oncologic implications, do you notice any changes in its size, color, or symmetry recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The non-healing, crusty nature of these lesions in a 62-year-old smoker raises concern for squamous cell carcinoma; could you describe the size, specific appearance, and if there is any pain or bleeding associated with the penile and finger lesions? Also, do you have any known history of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection or chronic exposure to arsenic?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the Penis and Digit. Given the non-healing, crusty nature of the lesions in a 62-year-old smoker with prior failed syphilis treatment, the clinical picture is highly suggestive of malignancy. I am requesting a biopsy of both lesions and a review of any available dermoscopic images to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other etiologies like chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis or rare infections.
